2607.13315.title: Meta-Learning Preferences for Multilingual LLM Alignment
2607.13315.paper_summary: Unequal availability of human preference data across languages poses a significant challenge for aligning large language models in multilingual settings. To address the lack of sufficient data in low-resource language alignment, we propose a meta-learning framework for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Direct Preference Optimization. By leveraging preference data from other languages, our framework learns a transferable initialization that enables effective adaptation to a target language with minimal data. We provide theoretical guarantees for both the meta-reward modeling and meta-policy optimization settings, and empirically demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on multilingual benchmarks. In an extremely low-resource setting with only 100 target-language preference samples, our approach achieves up to $28\%$ win-rate improvements over baseline methods, and consistently outperforms baselines across multiple target languages and model scales. Our approaches retain these advantages across different combinations of meta-training languages and varying linguistic distances from the target languages.
2607.13315.paper_summary_zh: 人類偏好數據在不同語言中的不平等可用性對於在多語言環境中對齊大型語言模型構成了重大挑戰。<lb/>為了解決低資源語言對齊中數據不足的問題，我們提出了一個元學習框架，用於從人類反饋中進行強化學習和直接偏好優化。<lb/>通過利用其他語言的偏好數據，我們的框架學習了一個可轉移的初始化，使其能夠在數據最少的情況下有效適應目標語言。<lb/>我們為元獎勵建模和元策略優化設置提供了理論保證，並在多語言基準上實證證明了我們方法的有效性。<lb/>在一個極低資源的環境中，只有100個目標語言的偏好樣本，我們的方法在基準方法上實現了高達$28\%$的勝率提升，並在多個目標語言和模型規模上持續超越基準。<lb/>我們的方法在不同的元訓練語言組合和與目標語言的語言距離變化中保持了這些優勢。
